annotation.title_clean: Using Fitts' Law to Benchmark Assisted Human-Robot Performance
annotation.title_en: Using Fitts' Law to Benchmark Assisted Human-Robot Performance
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Pan, J.; Eden, J.; Oetomo, D.; Johal, W.
annotation.summary_en: Technical human-robot collaboration paper proposing a Fitts' Law-based benchmark for shared-control teleoperation. A user study (N=24) shows task difficulty and robot autonomy level affect performance, cognitive load and trust. It has no governance content, though the benchmark could support assessing shared-control quality.
key_provisions_or_claims: Proposes an adapted Fitts' Law as a benchmark for shared-control reaching tasks.
Task difficulty and robot autonomy both affect movement time, with higher autonomy reducing the difficulty effect.
Perceived cognitive load (NASA-TLX) and trust (MDMT) are influenced by difficulty and autonomy.
Task difficulty could serve as a proxy for real-time cognitive load estimation.
